chunks: "I like to group them by what they do.
Compute blocks: one or more CPU cores with caches, often a GPU, and increasingly accelerators like a neural engine, a DSP, an image signal processor and a video codec.
Memory: on-chip SRAM, a boot ROM, in microcontrollers on-chip flash, and for bigger SoCs a DRAM controller and its PHY.
Then the interconnect, a bus matrix or network-on-chip, plus DMA engines and an interrupt controller so the CPU doesn't have to babysit every transfer.
Peripherals and I/O: GPIO, UART, SPI, I2C, timers, ADCs, then high-speed stuff like USB, PCIe, Ethernet, MIPI camera and display interfaces.

Infrastructure that people forget: PLLs and clock trees, reset logic, a power management unit with multiple voltage and clock domains, security blocks like a crypto engine, secure boot and key storage, and debug access over JTAG or SWD.
All of that is wired into one address map, so software controls it through registers.
Which blocks a particular SoC has depends on the product: a sensor MCU has a core, flash, SRAM, ADC and a radio, a phone processor has a big CPU cluster, GPU, NPU, ISP and a modem."
